decision: DRAFT (Brian to confirm): can a tennis-ball-sized foam ball with a 28 mm speaker be heard clearly over a lively Christmas-morning room, well enough to justify building a prototype?

dimensions.title: Is the ball heard where it matters?

results.claim: A full scream at 3 m in the living room is at least 10 dB above the room's background, enough to be understood.
results.source: Speech is understood reliably about 10-15 dB above background noise (ANSI/ASA S12.60 asks 15 dB for classrooms).

results.claim: The murmur is audible at half a metre in a quiet room (40 dBA), at least 5 dB above it.
results.source: Product requirement: you should hear it fretting in your hand.

dimensions.title: Does the sim let Brian hear the answer for himself?

results.claim: Listening at the tripod with room noise on, Brian can make out what the ball yells.
results.why: In the sim (Christmas morning, Listener: phone on the tripod, room noise on, Volume so the room sounds real), throw the ball. Could you make out what it yelled?

dimensions.title: Are the sim's loudness inputs true to real parts and real rooms?

results.claim: The sim's 28 mm speaker is as loud as real 28 mm, 8 ohm, 1 W parts (dB SPL at 10 cm with 1 W).
results.source: Distributor listings, 2026-10-18: Taoglas SPKM.28.8.A 89 dB at 0.5 W / 10 cm (= 92 dB at 1 W); PUI Audio AS02808MR-R 80 dB at 1 W / 1 m (= 100 dB at 10 cm). Confirm in the PDF datasheets.

results.claim: The amp's power on battery voltage matches the MAX98357A's published figures into 8 ohms.
results.source: Adafruit MAX98357 guide: 0.8 W at 3.3 V and 1.8 W at 5 V into 8 ohms, 10% THD. 3.7 V lies between; 1.0 W is an interpolation, not a datasheet value.

results.claim: The sound lost through the shell (pink noise, A-weighted) matches a phone measurement of a real speaker wrapped in real foam.
results.why: waiting for your measurement "shell-loss-dba": See docs/MEASURING.md, test 2: pink noise from a small speaker, phone meter 30 cm away, open air then wrapped in foam; record open-air LAeq minus wrapped LAeq.

results.claim: The sim's Christmas-morning background (58 dBA) matches a real lively family room.
results.why: waiting for your measurement "room-noise-dba": See docs/MEASURING.md, test 1: phone meter on the table during a lively family moment, 60-second LAeq.

next: Fix "heard-at-3m" (behavior): A full scream at 3 m in the living room is at least 10 dB above the room's background, enough to be understood.
